name: Fogo Island Inn
positioning: Full-board inn on stilts on Fogo Island, off the north-east coast of Newfoundland, designed by architect Todd Saunders, furnished by island makers and run so that operating surpluses go back to the community
best_for: Travelers who want ocean-view rooms and guided hiking, kayaking and wildlife outings included in the stay
Guests who care about local craft, island culture and a stay whose surpluses support the community

facts.text: Fogo Island Inn sits on an island off the north-east coast of Newfoundland.
The inn's architect is Todd Saunders.
The rocks that adorn the inn's rooftop were gathered from the island.
Most guest rooms have wood stoves, and the public spaces have wood-burning fireplaces.
The inn's textile pieces were stitched, knitted, crocheted and hooked on Fogo Island.
Rates include the inn's services and experiences without hidden costs, tips or resort fees.
Breakfast, lunch and supper are included daily.
Guests have access to the inn's amenities, including a cinema, an art gallery and hot tubs.
Stays include outdoor guides and personalized itineraries for land excursions and hikes.
Stays include an island orientation with a Community Host.
Guests can sea kayak in the North Atlantic with the inn's Outdoor Adventure Guides.
Led by Executive Chef Tim Charles, the culinary team creates menus that shift with the seasons.

highlights.text: The inn's steel frame is anchored to bedrock on stilts sunk into the rock.
The rooms have floor-to-ceiling ocean views.
All operating surpluses are reinvested in the Fogo Island community through Shorefast.
The furniture in the inn is primarily handcrafted on Fogo Island at Fogo Island Workshops.
Winter offers glimpses of the island's caribou herd and of seals arriving on ice floes, and summer is the season for whale watching and for puffins nesting on the nearby Little Fogo Islands.

considerations.text: Getting there takes planning: from Gander there is a one-hour drive to the Farewell ferry terminal and then a 45-minute ferry to Fogo Island, and transport to and from the island costs extra.
A minimum stay of 3 nights is required, and a 4-night stay is recommended.
Children aged 8 and older are welcome to stay.
